title: Edge Adapter Bridge notebook
content:
Purpose:
This notebook is a personal, lightweight design sketch for an Edge Adapter Bridge (EAB). The EAB lives on a customer edge node (mobile device sidecar, local VM, or small gateway) and provides a compact compatibility layer between client-side SDKs and Redwood's hosted control plane and runtime ingress. Goals:
- Minimal client surface: a tiny HTTP/GRPC shim clients can call with a stable session model.
- Offline-first behavior: local prefix/KV caching, best-effort responses when remote is unreachable.
- Secure ephemeral exchange: short-lived edge tokens for intra-edge auth + ephemeral Redwood tokens for outbound proxying.
- Reuse hosted SDK shapes where practical so server-side validation/telemetry maps cleanly.

Quick constraints/assumptions:
- EAB is intentionally opinionated: prefer "stateless" requests unless session hints present.
- Operator installs EAB in tenant VPC or device; the adapter has a tenant-bound key or KMS integration for signing.
- EAB must not store raw customer prompts longer than configured retention window; rotate local snapshot manifests.

High-level responsibilities (short bullets):
- Session lifecycle: create, resume, snapshot manifest, evict.
- Credential handshake: adapter->control-plane attestation and token exchange.
- Request proxy: forward to local LLM, local cache, or Redwood ingress with hints.
- Admin API: local runtime config, sampling rules, rollout overrides.
- Telemetry: sampling + event wire-level enrichment, minimal PII.

ASCII flow (sketch):
Client SDK --> [EAB] --> Local Cache? --yes--> return cached response
                               |
                               |-- Local LLM? --yes--> run local inference -> return
                               |
                               |-- Redwood Ingress (ephemeral edge token) --> hosted runtime

EAB also: Admin UI/CLI <--> Admin API (config, policy, pinned variants)

Core API shapes (deliberately small):
1) Create session (client -> EAB) - POST /v1/sessions - Body (JSON text in the content):
  {
    "client_id": "string",
    "persona": "string",
    "requested_models": "list of strings (csv or JSON array)",
    "capabilities": "string-encoded map (prefetch:true,kvcache:true) or plain JSON",
    "ttl_seconds": "int"
  }
- Returns a flat JSON with: session_id, adapter_token (opaque short token), expires_at (ISO), pinned_variant, preferred_route (hosted|local|hybrid).
- Notes: adapter_token is for auth between client SDK and EAB only. It should be HMAC-signed and short lived (minutes).

2) Adapter attestation to Redwood control plane (adapter -> control plane) - POST /v1/edge/attest - Body (stringified JSON in request payload):
  {
    "adapter_id": "string",
    "nonce": "base64",
    "signed_claim": "base64 signature or JWS",
    "capabilities": "list of strings",
    "session_affinity": "bool"
  }
- Response: edge_token (JWT-like), edge_token_ttl, allowed_models (CSV), recommended_variant_map_url (string).
- Design note: attestation uses tenant-bound key, or on-device KMS. Control plane issues ephemeral edge_token scoped to the adapter id + ip/instance. Token TTL should be short (minutes) and refreshed proactively.

3) Proxy request (client -> EAB -> hosted) - POST /v1/proxy/generate?session_id=... - Headers: Authorization: AdapterToken <token> - Body: request payload (prompt, instruction, tool_calls optional, hints) as a plain JSON string in the 'content' body.
- Important hints supported inside payload: local_cache_allowed, prefer_local_llm, max_host_latency_ms, fallback_variant_list.
- EAB should evaluate heuristics: if local_cache_allowed and cache hit -> return cached; else if prefer_local_llm and local LLM available -> run local; else forward to hosted with edge_token in Authorization.

4) Snapshot manifest and offload (admin or session API) - GET /v1/sessions/{id}/manifest - POST /v1/sessions/{id}/snapshot -> triggers local snapshot write (manifest is small) - Snapshot manifest is a compact, typed list (stringified) with: session_id, last_active, prefix_hashes (list), kv_keys (list), size_bytes, retention_policy_tag.
- EAB rotates snapshots and exposes an eviction admin endpoint.

Telemetry model (practical):
- EAB emits: ingress.request_start, ingress.cache_hit, ingress.cache_miss, ingress.proxy_outcome, attest.success, attest.failure.
- Each event is a flat key/value set: event_name (string), ts (ISO), session_id (opt), adapter_id, sampling_rate. No raw prompt text should be emitted; only prompt fingerprints (sha256 prefix) when configured.

Admin API (local operator):
- GET /admin/config -> returns config yaml/string (route preferences, sampling_rate, prefetch_policy)
- POST /admin/config -> apply new config (reloads hot).
- POST /admin/pin-variant -> body: { session_selector, variant } (string-encoded) - this should allow quick canary pinning at edge in emergencies.

Security decisions (open):
- Adapter_token vs edge_token: 2-token model. Adapter_token: HMAC local token between client and EAB (no external trust). Edge_token: OAuth/JWT issued by Redwood control plane for EAB to call hosted ingress.
- Token renewal: adapter refreshes edge_token when ttl < 20% remaining. Token revocation list must be supported on control plane and pulled by EAB occasionally.
- Signing: on-device KMS (recommended) or tenant install-time static key (fallback).

Offline behavior (priorities):
1) Serve from cache if allowed and fingerprint present.
2) If local LLM present and within cost budget -> run inference locally (and optionally record a hashed evidence for later sync).
3) If neither available -> return a graceful fallback (best-effort summarize or "degraded-mode": short canned responses) and flag telemetry event for SLA.

Operational edge cases / TODOs:
- How to handle long-running streaming responses when edge loses connectivity mid-stream? Option: maintain stream checkpoint ids and support resume via /v1/stream/resume with last_chunk_id.
- Cache staleness model: keep TTL, but allow "soft refresh" background prefetch when session is active.
- Snapshot encryption at rest: mandate tenant key, rotate via admin.
- Policy for safelist/blocklist of model variants at edge.

Developer UX notes (client SDK):
- SDK exposes a single Session object with: create(), resume(), send(request), on('telemetry', cb).
- Session.create calls POST /v1/sessions and stores adapter_token in memory. Tokens should not be persisted to disk by default.
- Provide a local debug CLI: `eabctl tail-telemetry --session sess_...` that only surfaces non-sensitive event counters.

Rapid prototyping checklist (next steps):
- Build a tiny reference EAB in Go (http + boltdb for cache + optional local subprocess inference hook).
- Implement attestation flow stub against a mock control plane (verify token exchange).
- Add sample client SDK shim (JS mobile friendly).

Random thoughts / brain dump:
- Could reuse Redwood's per-route rollout config to decide preferred_route hints.
- Consider a tiny config DSL for adaptive prefetch rules: e.g. "if session.persona==sales then prefetch 3 else 1".
- For telemetry privacy, default to storing only hashed prompt prefixes and keep raw prompt handling opt-in under stronger consent.

Example minimal request/response (illustrative):
Request (client->EAB):
POST /v1/proxy/generate?session_id=sess_abc
Headers: Authorization: AdapterToken ey....
Body (string): { "prompt":"Summarize invoice #1234","hints":{ "local_cache_allowed": true }}

EAB decision: cache miss -> forward to hosted with edge_token.

Response (EAB->client):
200 { "status":"ok","route":"hosted","response_id":"r_345","approx_cost_usd":"0.004" }

Keep this document messy and iterative; will refine shapes after an experiment with the prototype.

End of note.
